## Operator-split pieces at the step boundary: saturation adjustment, chemistry and radial conduction (`thermo.reactions`) {#sec-ch09-split}

### Summary

The dynamics advance the conserved state over the whole step; the phase equilibrium of @sec-ch02 then adjusts the
species at fixed density and internal energy density, the chemistry step integrates the reaction rates over the
step on the refreshed primitives, and the physical boundaries are refilled so the ghosts carry the new
composition. All of this is inside the last stage. Each piece sees the output of the previous one, which makes the
step a sequential split. The details of the phase solve and the kinetics are @sec-ch10. One source is split
symmetrically instead: the implicit radial conduction of @sec-ch07-csdiffusion takes half a step before the stages
and half a step after them.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Applies the phase equilibrium and then the chemistry to the advanced state; @eq-ch09-split-lie.

**Data.** Reads the state after the last average; writes the species densities $\rho_n$, with $E$ kept by the phase step.

**Placement.** Last stage, after the average: saturation, chemistry, boundary fill; a Mesh runs the chemistry in its global phase.

**Activation.** Saturation adjustment when the thermo card has reactions; chemistry when the driver sets a kinetics model.

**Guarantee / limits.** First order in $\Delta t$ (a sequential, or Lie, split) unless the pieces commute.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch09-split-tests; `test_wall_saturation.release`, `test_sk4_chemistry_source_python`, `split_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C4]`.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{dyn}}_{\Delta t}$ is the dynamics over one step (all Runge-Kutta stages),
$\mathcal S$ the saturation adjustment and $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{kin}}_{\Delta t}$ the chemistry step; on a linear model
$\mathcal M^{\mathrm{dyn}}_{\Delta t}=e^{\Delta t\,\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}}$ and $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{kin}}_{\Delta t}=e^{\Delta t\,\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}}$
with generators $\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}$, $\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}$ [s$^{-1}$], and
$[\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}},\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}]=\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}-\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}$
is their commutator; $t_{\mathrm{end}}$ [s] is the length of a run. The phase equilibrium reads the total density $\rho$[^rg-3787dff4f9c4], the
internal energy density $\rho e$ and the mass fractions $y_n$[^rg-b518aee12bfe] of each interior cell; the chemistry reads the
post-adjustment temperature [K], pressure [Pa] and molar concentrations [mol m$^{-3}$].

### Derivation

One step is

$$
\mathbf U^{n+1} = \mathcal M^{\mathrm{kin}}_{\Delta t}\,\mathcal S\,\mathcal M^{\mathrm{dyn}}_{\Delta t}\,\mathbf U^n .
$$ {#eq-ch09-split-lie}

Why it is first order, on the linear model with the projection $\mathcal S$ left out:

1. Expanding both exponentials to second order,
   $e^{\Delta t\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}}e^{\Delta t\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}}=\mathsf I+\Delta t(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}+\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}})
   +\tfrac{\Delta t^2}2(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}^2+2\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}+\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}^2)+O(\Delta t^3)$.
   The exact flow is $e^{\Delta t(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}+\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}})}=\mathsf I+\Delta t(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}+\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}})
   +\tfrac{\Delta t^2}2(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}+\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}})^2+O(\Delta t^3)$.
2. The square of the sum is $\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}^2+\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}+\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}+\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}^2$,
   so the difference of the two lines is the local error
   $\tfrac{\Delta t^2}2(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}}\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}-\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}})
   =\tfrac{\Delta t^2}2[\mathsf G_{\mathrm{kin}},\mathsf G_{\mathrm{dyn}}]$ per step, zero when the generators commute (`[C4]`).
3. Over $t_{\mathrm{end}}/\Delta t$ steps the local errors add to $O(\Delta t)$, so the split is first order unless the
   operators commute.
4. *Round-off.* The split adds no arithmetic of its own: each piece rounds as its own section states (@sec-ch10),
   and the kinetics update first divides `del_conc` by `inv_mu`, then adds the result to `hydro_u`.
   These are two roundings per entry. With exact inputs, the first-order absolute error is at most
   $(\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2)(|\Delta\rho_n|+|\rho_n+\Delta\rho_n|)$; near cancellation this is not a relative bound on the new density.

On two non-commuting $2\times2$ generators the fitted order of this split is 0.991, a symmetric (Strang) split would
give 2.000 (`[C1]`, `[C2]`), and commuting generators split exactly, within the $10^{-14}$ check threshold in floating point (`[C3]`).
The saturation adjustment is a projection onto equilibrium rather than a flow over $\Delta t$, so its split error is
the error of applying equilibrium at the end of the step instead of throughout it.

**Not provided:** a measurement of that saturation-adjustment split error; the checks above use linear
generators rather than the equilibrium projection.

The physical boundary fill that follows the chemistry adds no update to the interior and is left out of
@eq-ch09-split-lie.

In the code, the $\mathcal S$ of @eq-ch09-split-lie is the last-stage `ThermoY` solve of the block, `pthermo`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_saturation >}}), and
$\mathcal M^{\mathrm{kin}}_{\Delta t}$ is `ChemistrySource::forward`
({{< code src/chemistry/chemistry_source.cpp ChemistrySource::forward >}}).

The radial conduction split is symmetric: with $\mathcal D_{\Delta t/2}$ the implicit radial step over half the step,
the step is $\mathcal D_{\Delta t/2}\,\mathcal M^{\mathrm{dyn}}_{\Delta t}\,\mathcal D_{\Delta t/2}$, the Strang order of `[C2]`.
It needs a dry ideal gas, so it never runs together with $\mathcal S$ or $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{kin}}_{\Delta t}$
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion_radial.cpp DiffusionImpl::radial_conduction_step >}}).

### Numerical method

See @fig-ch09-split-step for the order within a step.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-split-step
#| fig-cap: "The pieces of one step in the order they run: the Runge-Kutta stages (sky blue), then inside the last stage the saturation adjustment, the chemistry step (green) and the physical boundary fill, and the acceptance check (orange). Each piece acts on the result of the one before."
#| fig-alt: "Five boxes in a row joined by arrows: dynamics, saturation adjustment, chemistry, physical boundaries, check_redo."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.figures.fig_split_step import make_fig
make_fig()
```

1. At stage 0, before the step-start state is saved, each split source takes its first half step; at the last
   stage it takes the second half step right after the average, and a redo undoes the first
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_advance >}};
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_combine >}};
   {{< code src/forcing/diffusion_radial.cpp DiffusionImpl::begin_split overload=2 >}}). The only split source
   at the pin is the implicit radial conduction.
2. At the last stage, after the average and the conserved limiter, the `saturation` operation applies the limiter
   again, forms the internal energy density and mass fractions on interior cells and calls the kintera `ThermoY`
   solve, `pthermo`, with a warm start ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_saturation >}}).
3. The `chemistry` operation of a single block then refreshes the primitives from the adjusted state with
   `peos->forward`, evaluates the kinetics rates and their rate constants in one call,
   `forward_with_rate_constants`, forms the Jacobian from that call's rate constants and advances them with
   `evolve_implicit` over the full step ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_chemistry >}};
   {{< code src/chemistry/chemistry_source.cpp ChemistrySource::forward >}}). A block of a `Mesh` skips it there;
   the Mesh runs it for each block in its global phase, one block after another, and refills that block's
   boundaries ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}).
4. The `boundaries` operation fills the physical boundaries, so the wall ghosts carry the adjusted composition
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_boundaries >}}).
5. `check_redo` then decides on the whole step, chemistry included (@sec-ch09-redo).

: Code map of the step-boundary split. {#tbl-ch09-split-code}

**How to use it.** Neither moist piece has a key in this section. The saturation adjustment runs at the last stage
when the thermodynamics card has reactions (@sec-ch10-satadj), through this test
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_saturation >}}):

```cpp
  if (stage == pintg->stages.size() - 1 && phydro->options->eos()->thermo() &&
      phydro->options->eos()->thermo()->reactions().size() > 0) {
```

The chemistry runs only if the driver sets a kinetics model, as the example driver does before its loop
({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}):

```cpp
  block->set_chemistry(*kintera::KineticsOptionsImpl::from_yaml(infile));
```

and the update it applies is ({{< code src/chemistry/chemistry_source.cpp ChemistrySource::forward >}}):

```cpp
  auto del_conc = kintera::evolve_implicit(rate, kinet->stoich, jac, dt);
```

The guard is $\mathcal S$ of @eq-ch09-split-lie, applied once at the last stage; `evolve_implicit` is
$\mathcal M^{\mathrm{kin}}_{\Delta t}$, over the full step. A driver that does not call `set_chemistry` has no
$\mathcal M^{\mathrm{kin}}_{\Delta t}$, and a card without reactions makes the chemistry a no-op. Refused:
`set_chemistry` stops with "MeshBlock::set_chemistry needs an EOS[^rg-a70646e99981] with a thermo" on a block whose equation of
state has no thermodynamics ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::set_chemistry >}}); the reaction and
kinetics cards are read and checked by kintera (@sec-ch10).

The ctest cases pass at the pin (@tbl-ch09-ctest-run):
{{< code tests/test_wall_saturation.cpp WallSaturation.phase_change_preserves_energy_and_water >}},
{{< code tests/test_check_redo_saturation.py main >}}, {{< code tests/test_sk4_chemistry_source.py main >}},

`split_check.py` models the order of the pieces by two linear operators.[^ch09-split-run] `[C1]` measures errors
$1.63\times10^{-3}$, $8.26\times10^{-4}$, $4.15\times10^{-4}$ at 20, 40 and 80 steps (order 0.991); `[C2]` gives 2.000
for the symmetric order of the radial half steps; `[C3]` splits commuting operators within $10^{-14}$; `[C4]` checks
steps 1 and 2 symbolically on generic $2\times2$ generators. No test measures the split error of a moist case, and
the radial case tests the order of the radial step, not of the split around the stages.

### Limits

1. **First order.** The moist pieces are split sequentially, first order in $\Delta t$ whatever the order of the
   Runge-Kutta stages; no symmetric split is offered for them. Not measured on a moist case.
2. **The chemistry is set by the driver.** The chemistry runs only after `set_chemistry`; a driver that applies its
   own kinetics elsewhere changes the split. On a `Mesh` the blocks' chemistry runs one block after another in the
   global phase, not on the worker pool ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}).
3. **Non-convergence.** A phase solve that does not converge within its iteration limit is counted and rejects
   the step (@sec-ch09-redo). The count is drained once per check, so a failure counted between steps is not the
   step's.
4. **The radial half steps are not covered by the split check of a run.** No test measures the second order of the
   radial split around the stages on a full step; `[C2]` shows it on a linear model only.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-3787dff4f9c4]: $\rho$ — total density, dry plus every species that carries mass [kg m$^{-3}$]

[^rg-b518aee12bfe]: $y_n$ — mass fraction of species $n$ **per unit total mass**, $\rho_n = \rho y_n$, dimensionless [-]; this is snapy's composition variable and the only one the state vector carries

[^rg-a70646e99981]: EOS — equation of state
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
